sourceNotes: Approved “in full detail.” Do not rush the cumulative loss or turn it into a one-joke punchline.
imagePrompt: Create one 1536 x 1024 pixel painted scene sheet, EXACTLY TWO COLUMNS BY THREE ROWS, six equal-width WIDE cinematic panels in row-major order 0 to 5. Each column is 768 pixels; rows are approximately 341, 341 and 342 pixels high. Hard straight cell edges; no gutters, no panel labels, no numbers, no captions, no typography, no readable lettering, no logos. Every cell is its own complete environment, never a sprite or a cutout. Use the polished watercolor and fine ink on textured cream paper style of Enough: warm directional light, deep teal and umber shadows, restrained paper grain, expressive natural faces, subtle imperfect painted edges. Human anatomy is believable, heads naturally sized; shoulders, elbows, wrists, hands, hips and knees belong to one continuous body. Seat hips on the actual seat, feet on the same floor, fingers visibly holding their actual objects; no disembodied hands, duplicated limbs, floating props or pasted-on heads. Keep important faces, hands, contact points and grounded figures within each wide panel with safe margins. Maintain the same identities, clothing, figure scale, prop design and spatial continuity across all six scenes. Anonymous original visual casting only, not likenesses of credited storytellers. This is a dramatic storyboard adaptation, not a claim that imagined symbols or staged details are verified events. Story: The Winning Comment. Palette accents: #DEE8EB, #31465E, #EFAE59. Identity continuity: READER: The same adult man with tan skin, short dark brown hair, plain glasses, muted violet shirt and slate trousers; an ordinary book reviewer, never an evil caricature. Keep his actual chair, desk, keyboard and computer unchanged. SCREEN: An existing neutral offscreen system voice, not a visible character. Its notice is an abstract plain alert shape with no painted words. TOP LEFT (frame 0): An evening study with the reader seated properly at his desk, feet grounded, one hand resting on a keyboard and the other touching a familiar review notebook. Warm lamplight reveals an extensive orderly archive of anonymous booklike review volumes, separate notes and list folders climbing the shelves behind the computer. He surveys it with everyday familiarity. Establish the accumulated scale before any smirk or dramatic symbol; no readable titles or screen text. TOP RIGHT (frame 1): The same man leans toward the computer with a tight self-satisfied half-smile, both forearms naturally supported by the desk. One hand types deliberately while the other index finger hovers above a single blank send key; keep wrist, elbow and shoulder connected. A narrow thorn-like ink flourish curls only at the edge of the abstract comment bar. The full archive is still visible behind him, intact, creating a physical comparison between one sentence and years of work. MIDDLE LEFT (frame 2): The finger has just pressed the real keyboard key and the reader leans back a little, shoulders released in momentary triumph. A small plain ochre flag rises beside the abstract comment card, while a measured trail of a few card silhouettes travels across the screen area. His shelves, notes and lists remain fully intact in the same room. This is one petty winning moment, not a carnival of notifications or a villain's laugh. MIDDLE RIGHT (frame 3): A plain pale alert rectangle interrupts the small flag on the computer, bearing only a minimal neutral icon, no words. The reader leans forward with knitted brows, one hand on the mouse and the other reaching toward the nearest familiar archive shelf as its first row becomes translucent empty outlines. Other shelves, notes and lists remain legible as distinct stored categories. His face asks whether this is reversible; loss has begun but is not complete. BOTTOM LEFT (frame 4): The reader has risen halfway from his real chair, one hand braced on the desk and the other reaching toward separate fading notebook and list-folder compartments. Several shelves are now empty while the last row of booklike reviews thins to pale outlines. His glasses catch the screen light and his mouth is open in separate recognition of notes, lists and everything else. Keep vanished items ghosted only at their actual former positions; no crash, flying book storm or comic collapse. BOTTOM RIGHT (frame 5): All archive compartments are empty. The reader sits again in the same chair in a narrow pool of computer light, shoulders rounded and hands resting open on the desk without typing. One tiny thorn-shaped trace near his temple suggests how clearly he remembers the insult, contrasted with the large blank shelves where his work was. The screen has only a small vertical cursor mark, no moral, no restored account. His eyes move from recollection toward the lost archive; regret is quiet and specific. Story-specific safeguards: All eight existing dialogue lines remain full and in order, especially the final two separate admissions. Do not paint an insult, actual platform branding, policy wording or a generic moral; captions supply approved words. Do not erase the whole archive at the first notice or restore it at the end. This is a symbolic dramatization of accumulated value, not a new verified account of platform mechanics.
